claim: Demo sample data stays separate from real practice data.
sandbox: An isolated database inserts a non-demo practice fixture, then proves demo read and mutation requests both return 404 and the fixture remains unchanged.

claim: Demo tokens use 256 random bits and sample workspaces expire after 24 hours.
sandbox: Generates and parses a token, decodes 32 random bytes, checks the exact 24-hour TTL, and rejects an expired token.

claim: Demo writes allow 12 immediate requests per first forwarded client IP, then return a retry time of at least one second.
sandbox: An isolated router sends 13 writes from one X-Forwarded-For address, asserts the first 12 advertise limit 12, and asserts the thirteenth returns 429 with matching positive Retry-After headers while another forwarded client remains allowed.

claim: The sample opens without an account or payment.
sandbox: A fresh browser opens the complete seeded demo and records that no login, checkout, or payment request occurs.

claim: Reset demo starts a fresh set of sample bookings.
sandbox: Fresh /demo workspace changes the recovery state, selects Reset demo, asserts a new token and original states, then proves the old workspace returns 404.

claim: A recovery message needs recorded contact consent.
sandbox: Demo data includes one unfinished attempt without email consent. Attempting recovery leaves no outbound message in its case and shows the consent explanation.

claim: The demo shows a receipt after a sample recovery action.
sandbox: Fresh demo selects the consented unfinished booking, runs the accelerated sample recovery, and asserts a timestamped simulated email receipt and case outcome are visible.

claim: Demo does not contact payment, messaging, sign-in, or AI services.
sandbox: Playwright records every request for the full fresh-demo flow and asserts each URL is same-origin; no request is made to Stripe, a messaging provider, Entra, Sociobot billing, or the AI gateway.

claim: The one-click sample opens three fictional bookings.
sandbox: A fresh browser enters through /?demo=1, sees the persistent demo banner, and observes exactly three named sample booking tickets.

claim: A practice can create a private workspace and publish one paid-session page.
sandbox: A fresh browser creates a practice, receives a private access token, opens its recovery queue, follows its unique public URL, and observes the configured session and deposit.

claim: A booking records channel consent before opening hosted payment.
where: Public booking page, privacy page, README
sandbox: A clean practice receives a public booking with explicit email consent, the browser opens only its configured hosted payment URL, and the owner API shows the timestamped consent and awaiting-deposit state.

claim: Client contact fields are encrypted at rest and stay inside their practice.
sandbox: An isolated database creates two practices, stores a real-looking booking, proves raw name/email columns do not contain plaintext, decrypts them only for the owner, and proves the other practice sees no attempt.

claim: A practice owner can export its records and delete the complete practice.
sandbox: An isolated practice downloads its JSON export, deletes through the authenticated endpoint, then proves the database has no practice and the old key no longer opens it.

claim: A permitted recovery records provider status, and one email bounce can trigger one permitted SMS fallback.
sandbox: An isolated practice connects an in-process provider, sends one consented email, records an authenticated bounce receipt twice, and proves exactly one SMS fallback plus an auditable event timeline.

claim: A hosted payment return does not mark a deposit paid; only an authenticated provider event does.
sandbox: An isolated booking starts awaiting deposit, rejects an invalid callback token, accepts one authenticated paid event twice without duplication, and then shows paid in the owner record.

claim: An occupied session time cannot be booked twice.
sandbox: Two clients submit the same future time for one practice; the first succeeds, the second receives slot_unavailable, and one database record remains.

claim: An unpaid booking gets a durable automatic recovery, and withdrawn consent stops it.
sandbox: An isolated provider receives one accelerated due recovery. A second due job with consent withdrawn is marked stopped, and a second scheduler run creates no duplicate send.

claim: The service schedules a consented recovery message 15 minutes after an unpaid booking.
sandbox: A controlled isolated booking records the durable recovery due time and asserts it is exactly 15 minutes after creation, allowing only the test's measured clock interval.

claim: A verified deposit queues one durable session reminder.
where: README product workflow and recovery queue
sandbox: An isolated payment callback accepts one authenticated paid event and asserts the database contains exactly one queued session-reminder job.

claim: A real workspace stores practice settings, bookings, consent records, scheduled messages, and delivery receipts.
sandbox: An isolated practice creates a consented booking, scheduled recovery, and receipt, then checks the owner export contains each stated record type.

claim: The booking form has no card fields; payment card details stay on the practice’s hosted payment page.
sandbox: A fresh public booking page is inspected for the absence of card fields; the captured booking request is asserted to contain no card data before navigation to the configured hosted payment origin.

claim: A practice can send a delivery connection test without client data.
sandbox: An isolated local provider receives a connection-test payload with no recipient or client data, while the practice database remains free of new booking attempts.

claim: The $29 per month practice price and current checkout state are shown plainly.
sandbox: A fresh landing page exposes the exact monthly price, the currently unavailable checkout state, and a working setup link.
